issues.summary: DW-26's original write-up mislocated the root cause: it framed StartColumn==0 as a producer off-by-one on a line-leading code path and claimed prior corpora honour a 1-based contract. The VBA AST is intentionally 0-based (ANTLR; SourceLocation.cs:3); ParserOutputProjector.BuildLocation (line 431) projects it raw with no +1 while hardcoding the top-level to StartColumn=1 (line 115) and the schema requires minimum:1. HHC/Northwind validate only because they have no column-0 token, not by honouring 1-based.
issues.resolutionNote: Independently verified the 0-based AST + raw projection + hardcoded top-level=1. Rewrote DW-26 as an internal-0-based-vs-public-1-based convention MISMATCH at projection, with two mutually-exclusive golden-affecting fix options (normalise projection +1, or relax schema to minimum:0). Updated the test's Invariant-2b comments to the convention-mismatch framing. The pin itself (IsValid==false + StartColumn [minimum] + structural StartColumn==0) is unchanged — it pins the public-contract failure regardless of which layer fixes it.

issues.summary: An exact-count assertion (Assert.Single on the onLoad entry points) sat inside the CAPABILITY-LEVEL invariants block, though exactly-one-onLoad is a corpus-structure canary that a benign FE edit could break.
